task.name: Replay completed stories through prior-run selection before injection is enabled, so scoring weights and claim budgets are judged on evidence instead of instinct
task.story_text:
## Problem

Prior-run selection ships with weights and budgets chosen a priori: file overlap
10, directory overlap 4, domain 6, work-type 3, story tokens 2, pattern tokens
2, recency 2; at most 3 candidates per assembly; at most 5 rendered claims of
400 characters each. The corpus those weights will operate on now exists — 17
real summaries in this repository, 2 in the `hdp` adopter — but no selection has
ever been observed against it. Injection is about to be enabled on parameters
nobody has watched run.

Three pending design decisions hang on exactly this missing evidence:

- **Controlled pattern vocabulary.** `learned_patterns` tags are coined fresh
  every run — 58 distinct tags here plus 6 in `hdp`, zero reused, including the
  same concept slugged two ways in two repos (`fail-closed-capability-handling`
  vs `fail-closed-caller-mapping`). Tag tokens are matched against incoming
  story text, so drift may or may not matter. Whether a shared vocabulary is
  worth building depends on whether pattern matching ever contributes recall
  that file/domain/story signals did not already provide.
- **Cross-run recurrence linking.** The corpus holds the same lesson learned
  independently twice — fenced-envelope truncation in diagnose parsing (run
  `1a6b6e18d232`, issue #2216) and in preflight parsing (run `73d7de156730`,
  issue #2542) — with nothing connecting them. Whether recurrence detection is
  worth building depends on whether such siblings already co-surface for a
  story touching either parser.
- **Budget sizing.** Whether 3 candidates × 5 claims is the binding constraint,
  and whether weak claims actually crowd out strong ones in rendered output,
  is currently a guess.

## Acceptance criteria

- A replay runs a representative set of completed stories from both corpora
  through the real selection path (`select_prior_runs`) against a built index,
  recording per story: which entries matched, the score reasons that qualified
  each one, what was excluded and why, and the advisory text as it would have
  been rendered.
- A replay for a given story considers only summaries generated before that
  story ran, so results reflect what injection would actually have offered at
  the time.
- Each replayed story carries a recorded judgment of whether the rendered
  claims would have changed its plan, implementation, or verification — with
  the useful and useless cases enumerable individually, not only counted.
- The report answers, with numbers: how often each scoring signal was the
  qualifying one; whether the two fence-parsing summaries co-surface for a
  parser-touching story on file/domain signal alone; how often the candidate
  cap or the rendered-claim cap truncated something judged useful.
- The result is sufficient to decide each of the three deferred questions —
  controlled vocabulary, recurrence linking, budget sizing — without a further
  round of analysis.

## Example

A shape sufficient to decide on:

```
Prior-run selection replay — 14 stories (11 theforge, 3 hdp)

stories with ≥1 candidate offered        9/14
  qualifying signal (first reason)
    file_overlap        6
    dir_overlap         2
    domain_match        1
    pattern_match       0
    story_match         0

fence-parsing co-surface test (story touching diagnose_prompts.py):
  1a6b6e18d232 offered (file_overlap)   73d7de156730 offered (dir_overlap)  ✓ co-surfaced

rendered-claim budget:
  claims rendered 31, judged would-have-helped 12 (39%)
  useful claims displaced by earlier filler claims: 3   ← issue #2606 (claim quality)
  candidates dropped at cap that scored above an offered one: 0

verdict inputs:
  controlled vocabulary: pattern_match qualified 0 selections → defer
  recurrence linking:    siblings co-surfaced in 2/2 probes  → defer
  budgets:               claim quality, not budget size, is binding
```

## Notes

Deliberately scoped to measurement against the existing selector, not to
changing weights, prompts, or index structure. What to do with the numbers is
decided afterward.

findings.description: Running the new replay command against the TheForge corpus named by the report aborts with missing judgment for theforge/b122a93bf342/plan/24bfd6e03a58/dec2f2192b49.

The dev and review phase-input entries are bound to the same dictionary object rather than independent values, so any later code that adjusted one phase's recovered scope would silently alter the other phase's recorded inputs.

Only two of the twenty theforge run records persist a structured plan, so eighteen dev and eighteen review replays score with no file-overlap input and their rows report story_match or domain_match as the qualifying signal.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 1 derives one touched files list and uses it for plan, dev, and review, but the real callers use different phase-time inputs: plan_flow.py:926-930 passes state.preflight_likely_files, while dev_phase.py:1205-1209 and review_phase.py:2559-2563 pass plan_file_list(state.plan_structured). Substituting completed-run changed_files leaks post-implementation evidence into the 10-point file and 4-point directory signals, so the replay will not reproduce what selection could have offered.
  Suggestion: Reconstruct and record the actual file list separately for each phase from persisted preflight and structured-plan artifacts; use None when the live phase used no list, and explicitly mark stories whose historical input cannot be recovered instead of substituting final changed files.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 1 rebuilds the index once at the corpus's current HEAD and then filters entries by timestamp. knowledge_index.py:_cited_source_facts and _materialize_source_fact compare each summary's baseline with current HEAD, so later source changes can exclude or down-rank a summary that was admissible when the replayed story began. Timestamp filtering alone therefore does not satisfy the historical replay criterion.
  Suggestion: For each replay, build the filtered index in a temporary Git worktree checked out at the replay story's pre-run changed_files.base_ref, populated only with summaries and authoritative run records generated before timing.started_at, then invoke the unchanged selector there.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] The first stated corpus risk is carried. Although explicit roots and exact reported counts handle corpus-count drift, rebuild_knowledge_index(project_root) writes to the supplied corpus at knowledge_index.py:162-201. The available /Users/pwickersham/src/hdp corpus is readable but outside this worktree's writable roots, so the planned two-corpus command will fail before producing the required report.
  Suggestion: Materialize each corpus in a writable temporary worktree or clone before rebuilding its index, preserving the Git history, summaries, and authoritative run records needed for admissibility. Add a test proving replay leaves input corpus roots unchanged.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 1's temporal cutoff materializes 'a temporary project root containing only index entries whose generated_at is before ...', but _render_summary (prior_run_selector.py:432-441) resolves prose from project_root / entry['summary_path']. An index-only temp root will render nothing and every candidate will be dropped as summary_unreadable, silently zeroing the advisory-text and claim-budget measurements.
  Suggestion: Materialize the temp root with the surviving summary artifacts at their original relative paths (copy or symlink .forge/knowledge/summaries/*.yaml), or filter the summary directory and call rebuild_knowledge_index on the temp root instead of hand-filtering entries. Add a Step 4 assertion that at least one replay yields non-empty candidate content.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 1 calls rebuild_knowledge_index(project_root), which unconditionally writes .forge/knowledge/index.yaml into the given root (knowledge_index.py:158-215). Pointed at the live TheForge or hdp checkout, the replay dirties the project root — no index.yaml exists there today, and a dirty root is a landing precondition failure for later sprints.
  Suggestion: Rebuild into the per-replay temp root only, and leave the source corpora untouched; if the real root must be read, copy summaries out first.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Carried risk (plan risk 1): the hdp corpus is not reachable from this workspace (a prior plan records the same limitation, and only 20 local summaries exist here), so AC 1's 'both corpora' cannot be satisfied in this environment. The plan's mitigation — explicit corpus roots, clear failure on a missing root, exact roots and counts stated in the report — makes the gap honest rather than closing it.
  Suggestion: Keep the mitigation as written and have the report state plainly that hdp was not replayed and which conclusions therefore rest on the TheForge corpus alone; do not fabricate hdp rows. If an hdp checkout is reachable at dev time, pass its root and replay it.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 1 says 'derive story text, touched files, started_at' from the paired run record, but the audit run JSON has no top-level story key — story shape lives under task (and the replayed story's own summary carries changed_files). The exact source fields are unstated.
  Suggestion: Pin the derivation explicitly (e.g. story text from task, file list from the story's own summary changed_files) and record it in the report so the replay's inputs are reproducible.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 2 is labelled Action: modify but two of its three files (src/theforge/prior_run_replay_render.py, src/theforge/cli/prior_run_replay.py) do not exist; only src/theforge/cli/main.py is a modification.
  Suggestion: No functional impact — register the new subcommand alongside knowledge_report in cli/main.py:21/93/137 as the plan already describes.

finding_registry.description: Running the new replay command against the TheForge corpus named by the report aborts with missing judgment for theforge/b122a93bf342/plan/24bfd6e03a58/dec2f2192b49.

The dev and review phase-input entries are bound to the same dictionary object rather than independent values, so any later code that adjusted one phase's recovered scope would silently alter the other phase's recorded inputs.

Only two of the twenty theforge run records persist a structured plan, so eighteen dev and eighteen review replays score with no file-overlap input and their rows report story_match or domain_match as the qualifying signal.

The fence-parsing co-surface probe queries prior-run selection with a candidate limit of 999 instead of the budget production assembly applies, so the probe anchored on the preflight-parser story reports the two fence-parsing summaries as co-surfacing even though the diagnose-parser summary ranks sixth and would never be offered under the real three-candidate budget.

A test replays the live repository knowledge corpus against the committed judgment file, and because the replay fails closed on any claim that has no recorded judgment, the test starts failing as soon as an unrelated story commits a new knowledge summary into the tracked corpus.

The repository-corpus replay test returns early without asserting anything once the judgment file no longer enumerates exactly the run ids present in the tracked knowledge corpus, so after the next completed story commits a new summary the test passes while the replay command itself refuses with a coverage error.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
